payload.text: Where the harness fixes a capture time, it states the machine and measurement it came from, because settling is a property of the ENVIRONMENT as much as the content and a value measured on one box is a lucky constant elsewhere. Converge-until-two-frames-agree is the preferred shape and is to be decided on that merit alone -- NOT as a fix for the crossfade misdiagnosis that prompted it, which AC-2.13 addresses instead. Its cost is named: convergence and the transition are the same phenomenon, so a converge loop settles correctly on a crossfade but on a CRAWL only after the animation ends, which is past the dwell. The bound therefore does real work and hitting it is common rather than exceptional.
